items.headline: Shoalhaven eyes a capped former landfill for a community solar-and-battery energy hub
items.summary: Shoalhaven City Council (NSW) has endorsed a draft plan of management identifying a remediated, clay-capped former landfill at North Nowra (an 11.36 ha site closed since 1979) as suitable for renewable-energy infrastructure, including a solar array and battery storage. The Council frames it as turning a long-term liability into a productive community asset and intends to lease the site to a renewable-energy provider, with two rounds of statutory consultation with Crown Lands and the NSW EPA still to run before the land can be used.
items.so_what: Many Australian councils sit on remediated former landfill and other constrained Crown or community land that cannot be built on but can host solar and storage. The transferable pattern here is the governance model — a plan of management that reclassifies a capped tip for electricity generation, then leases it to an energy operator for both a local renewable benefit and a council income stream — a climate/asset play any council with a closed landfill could examine, though it remains an early-stage proposal rather than a proven build.
